title: Decide whether recovery is real
description: After the open wait expires, choose a dependency condition, probe sample, and recovery contract. Full traffic returns only when every selected boundary passes.
modelNotice: Probe outcomes are deterministic fixtures for learning. A real breaker measures actual permitted calls and must synchronize concurrent state transitions.

profiles.label: Still failing
profiles.detail: The dependency has not recovered after the wait.

profiles.label: Partial recovery
profiles.detail: Most probes work, but capacity and latency remain unstable.

profiles.label: Sustained recovery
profiles.detail: The dependency handles representative probes within its budget.

profiles.label: Flapping dependency
profiles.detail: Latency looks acceptable, but intermittent failures remain.

policies.label: Strict recovery
policies.detail: Require zero failures, at most 10% slow probes, and p95 at or below 500 ms.
policies.consequence: Any failed or materially slow probe reopens the circuit.

policies.label: Balanced recovery
policies.detail: Allow at most 10% failures, 30% slow probes, and p95 at or below 800 ms.
policies.consequence: The dependency needs another open interval before more probes.

policies.label: Permissive recovery
policies.detail: Allow at most 25% failures, 50% slow probes, and p95 at or below 1500 ms.
policies.consequence: Even the permissive contract rejects this recovery sample.
